payload.claim: create_task now performs two separate appends for one task: task_created is committed and appended via _commit_and_append (line 1664), and only after that call returns does a second, independent self._append write run_created (line 1667). If the record refuses or errors on this second append (a RefsRecord push failure is a realistic cause, not just a contrived refusal), create_task raises after the task's SQL row and task_created fact are already durably committed. The task is then fully live and functional, but its record permanently lacks run_created, so every future fold will treat it as a bare task eligible to share a runs row by base_sha with other tasks, exactly the collapsing behavior b-cafacd set out to fix. finish_run's identical commit-then-append risk is explicitly tested (test_a_refused_run_finished_raises_after_the_runs_status_is_written), but no test exercises the record refusing run_created specifically, so this gap in the core invariant 'a task holding either run fact folds onto a run of its own' is undetected.
